raw_response:
Let me think this through as the farmer.

---

*Okay, let me think about this year. I'm 57, been on these 9.8 mu for 25 years, so I pretty much know what to do. My old man works construction in town when the work comes, and my daughter-in-law helps in the busy season. Mostly it's me in the fields.*

*Same as always — wheat in the fall, maize after. That's what everybody does here in Quzhou. I'm not going to switch to cotton or vegetables now, I'm too old to learn something new and who would I sell to.*

**Wheat** (already in the ground since October, about to head out)

My wheat is already up. I put in the regular seed I buy from the shop in town — nothing fancy, same kind the village uses. At planting I put down about one bag of compound fertilizer per mu (the 15-15-15 kind, 50 kg bag), that's what my neighbor and I have always done. In town they sometimes say use less, but I'm scared the wheat will be thin.

Now it's spring, the wheat is jointing. I'll irrigate once now — the well water is expensive because of the electricity, but if I don't water now the heads will be small. Then I'll broadcast some urea with the water, maybe half a bag per mu, so about 15 kg. If the wheat looks yellow after that I'll put a little more, but usually it's fine.

I'll irrigate again when the grain is filling, that's maybe late May. Three times total counting the winter water. For weeds I spray once with the stuff from the agro-shop, they tell me which one.

If the weather is good like last year I might get 400 kg per mu, sometimes 420. Bad year like the dry spring three years back, I only got 300.

**Maize** (plant right after wheat harvest in June)

As soon as the combine finishes the wheat in early June I need to plant maize fast — the ground can't sit. My son-in-law's cousin has a no-till planter he runs for the village, I pay him about 25 yuan a mu and he puts the seed and the compound fertilizer down in one pass, right into the wheat stubble. Hybrid seed from the shop, I don't save maize seed, everybody says the saved seed gives poor ears.

One bag of compound per mu at planting. Then when the maize is knee-high, around late July, I broadcast urea — about half a bag per mu — before a rain or an irrigation so it washes in. If it doesn't rain by then I have to pump from the well, which costs me. Usually in a normal year I only irrigate maize once or twice because the summer rains come.

Spray herbicide once early, that's enough. Bugs aren't usually a big problem for me.

Harvest end of September, hire the combine again, sell most of it, keep some for us and the chickens. Yield maybe 450 kg per mu if the rain is right.

**What I worry about**

Money is tight. My man's town wages come and go. I buy fertilizer on credit from the shop sometimes and pay when I sell the grain. I can't afford to put on a lot more fertilizer than this, and I can't afford to put on a lot less either — if the yield drops I lose more than I save.
